subject: Pricing and channel margin for dual-cloud private offer
messages:
From: Alex Park <procurement@cloudscale.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudScale Legal <legal@cloudscale.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Request: combined Azure+GCP private offer pricing + channel margin breakdown

Hi Maya / Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're moving toward a dual-cloud private offer (Azure + GCP) for a pilot across two lines of business and need a clear pricing sheet we can share with our procurement and reseller team. Specifically we need: 
- Per-cloud list price and committed-discount tiers (12/36/60 month)
- Suggested channel margin / reseller pass-through by cloud (we need to quantify impact on our seller economics)
- Any floor/ceiling language you require for marketplace private offers

I've attached the RFP with usage profile and projected ARR. Ideal timeline: receive a draft PO and summary by early next week (we're on a procurement deadline). Also confirm whether Redwood can issue an itemized invoice that preserves reseller margin lines for our channel partner invoice flow.

Attachments: CloudScale_RFP.pdf (usage profile + required terms)

Thanks,
Alex Park
Director, Procurement
CloudScale Inc
procurement@cloudscale.com

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: combined Azure+GCP private offer pricing + channel margin breakdown

Alex —

Appreciate the RFP. Quick summary and next steps below. I've attached a first-pass matrix (RI_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx) with list prices, commit tiers, and two channel-margin scenarios. High-level:

- Baseline suggestion: 12% reseller margin on Azure private offers, 10% on GCP private offers (applies to net-of-discount list price).
- Early-commit uplift: for 36+ month commitments we can add a 2–3% uplift to reseller margin to incentivize sellers — alternate scenario included in tab "Commit-Uplift".
- Floor clause proposal: reseller margin guarantee of 10% guaranteed for the term, with an annual true-up if list price adjustments reduce margin below that floor. This helps your channel economics remain predictable.
- Itemized invoicing: yes, Redwood can provide an itemized invoice with per-cloud line items and a reseller margin field for pass-through. We'll need your partner billing ID to map the lines properly.

Next steps: Ben (copied) will confirm tax treatment and marketplace pass-through mechanics. Can you confirm expected ARR and whether the partner will be a registered reseller on both Azure and GCP marketplaces? Once confirmed we'll return a draft PO and DocuSign-ready agreement.

Attachments: RI_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (pricing + two channel scenarios)

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <procurement@cloudscale.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: combined Azure+GCP private offer pricing + channel margin breakdown

Thanks Maya. Alex — a couple quick operational clarifications from partner ops:

- Tax + passthrough: We treat reseller margin as a gross margin line on the invoice; tax treatment depends on your reseller's jurisdiction. Irene, can you flag any complications for CloudScale if they are US-based but reselling internationally?
- Marketplace registration: For Azure private offers we need the partner to be a registered CSP/reseller and provide the partner ID; for GCP we need the reseller account mapped to the private offer. If CloudScale isn't registered on either, there are onboarding windows that could push timelines by 2–3 weeks.
- Alternate margin waterfall: if CloudScale needs to preserve seller economics at a 12% floor on both clouds, we can run a concession model where Redwood absorbs a 1–2% sponsor credit for the first 12 months in exchange for a longer commit (36 months). See tab "Sponsor-Credit" in Maya's matrix.

I'll coordinate with Irene on invoicing templates and tax notes. Maya — should I prepare the DocuSign-ready PO and send to Alex once legal confirms language?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
ben@redwood.com

From: Alex Park <procurement@cloudscale.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudScale Legal <legal@cloudscale.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 11:46:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Request: combined Azure+GCP private offer pricing + channel margin breakdown

Maya / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. We reviewed internally: overall this looks workable. A few points before we move to signature:

1) Channel margin floor: we need a guaranteed reseller margin of no less than 10% for the full term across both Azure and GCP. The sponsor-credit model is acceptable for year 1 if we commit to 36 months; please include the Sponsor Credit schedule in the PO.
2) Itemized invoice: confirmed — please include a per-cloud line, a reseller-margin line, and a partner billing ID field so we can pass straight through to our reseller sellers.
3) PO language: attached is our draft PO with standard CloudScale procurement clauses. Can Redwood return a DocuSign link with the draft PO + Sponsor Credit addendum?

Attachments: CloudScale_PO_Draft_v2.pdf

If you can return DocuSign by EOD Tuesday we'll be able to meet our internal acceptance window.

Thanks,
Alex Park
Director, Procurement
CloudScale Inc
procurement@cloudscale.com

On a process note — Ben, Irene: please call out any gating items that would delay the DocuSign (e.g., partner registration backlog, legal redlines).
